message.content:
Since \(27 \cdot 3 = 81 \equiv 1 \pmod{40}\), the inverse of \(27\) modulo \(40\) is \(3\).

Multiply both sides of
\[
27a \equiv 17 \pmod{40}
\]
by \(3\):
\[
a \equiv 17 \cdot 3 \equiv 51 \equiv 11 \pmod{40}.
\]

So the positive integers satisfying the congruence are
\[
11,\ 51,\ 91,\dots
\]

The smallest is \(11\), and the second-smallest is \(51\). Their sum is
\[
11+51=62.
\]

The answer is 62.
